case_studies.abstract: The emergence of LLM-driven information services is reshaping the conditions under which public knowledge institutions operate, threatening to absorb the editorial function these institutions exist to exercise. case_studies.title: SAG: SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation with Query-Time Dynamic Hyperedges
case_studies.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) offers an effective approach for large language models to access external knowledge. However, existing methods rely on dense similarity retrieval and face inherent limitations in handling structured constraints and multi-hop reasoning. Incorporating knowledge graphs partially alleviates these issues, but at the cost of semantic fragmentation, high maintenance overhead, and difficult incremental updates. case_studies.title: Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
case_studies.abstract: When large language models serve as evaluators in multi-agent systems, their systematic evaluation biases propagate through the agent network. We introduce Contagion Networks, a formal framework for measuring how evaluator biases spread across interacting LLM agents. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluator bias propagation in multi-agent large language model systems by introducing Contagion Networks, a framework for measuring bias spread. The team built a controlled experiment with three agents and found that evaluator biases consistently propagate between agents. The result shows that biases can spread even within the same underlying model.

case_studies.title: Optimal Order of Multi-Agent and General Many-Body Systems
case_studies.abstract: This paper develops a general framework for analyzing multi-agent systems with feedback loops between agents actions and collective observations. The framework is built on two fundamental agent-level variables: power, which measures agent influence on collective outcomes, and response functions, which determine how agents react to observations. We derive how macroscopic properties, including total power, useful power, entropy, order, fragility, and mobility, emerge from these two variables of heterogeneous agents.
